source_text: Ὅθεν καὶ ἐπιμένει ὁ θεὸς τὴν σύγχυσιν καὶ κατάλυσιν τοῦ παντὸς κόσμου μὴ ποιῆσαι, ἵνα καὶ οἱ φαῦλοι ἄγγελοι καὶ δαίμονες καὶ ἄνθρωποι μηκέτι ὦσι, διὰ τὸ σπέρμα τῶν Χριστιανῶν, ὃ γινώσκει ἐν τῇ φύσει ὅτι αἴτιόν ἐστιν. Ἐπεὶ εἰ μὴ τοῦτο ἦν, οὐκ ἂν οὐδὲ ὑμῖν ταῦτα ἔτι ποιεῖν καὶ ἐνεργεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν φαύλων δαιμόνων δυνατὸν ἦν, ἀλλὰ τὸ πῦρ τὸ τῆς κρίσεως κατελθὸν ἀνέδην πάντα διέκρινεν, ὡς καὶ πρότερον ὁ κατακλυσμὸς μηδένα λιπὼν ἀλλ᾿ ἢ τὸν μόνον σὺν τοῖς ἰδίοις παρ᾿ ἡμῖν καλούμενον Νῶε, παρ᾿ ὑμῖν δὲ Δευκαλίωνα, ἐξ οὗ πάλιν οἱ τοσοῦτοι γεγόνασιν, ὧν οἱ μὲν φαῦλοι, οἱ δὲ σπουδαῖοι. Οὕτω γὰρ ἡμεῖς τὴν ἐκπύρωσίν φαμεν γενήσεσθαι, ἀλλ᾿ οὐχ, ὡς οἱ Στωϊκοί, κατὰ τὸν τῆς εἰς ἄλληλα πάντων μεταβολῆς λόγον, ὃ αἴσχιστον ἐφάνη· ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ καθ᾿ εἱμαρμένην πράττειν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἢ πάσχειν τὰ γινόμενα, ἀλλὰ κατὰ μὲν τὴν προαίρεσιν ἕκαστον κατορθοῦν ἢ ἁμαρτάνειν, καὶ κατὰ τὴν τῶν φαύλων δαιμόνων ἐνέργειαν τοὺς σπουδαίους, οἷον Σωκράτην καὶ τοὺς ὁμοίους, διώκεσθαι καὶ ἐν δεσμοῖς εἶναι, Σαρδανάπαλον δὲ καὶ Ἐπίκουρον καὶ τοὺς ὁμοίους ἐν ἀφθονίᾳ καὶ δόξῃ δοκεῖν εὐδαιμονεῖν. Ὃ μὴ νοήσαντες οἱ Στωϊκοὶ καθ᾿ εἱμαρμένης ἀνάγκην πάντα γίνεσθαι ἀπεφήναντο. Ἀλλ᾿ ὅτι αὐτεξούσιον τό τε τῶν ἀγγέλων γένος καὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὴν ἀρχὴν ἐποίησεν ὁ θεός, δικαίως ὑπὲρ ὦν ἂν πλημμελήσωσι τὴν τιμωρίαν ἐν αἰωνίῳ πυρὶ κομίσονται. Γενητοῦ δὲ παντὸς ἥδε ἡ φύσις, κακίας καὶ ἀρετῆς δεκτικὸν εἶναι· οὐ γὰρ ἂν ἦν ἐπαινετὸν οὐδὲν αὐτῶν, εἰ οὐκ ἂν ἐπ᾿ ἀμφότερα τρέπεσθαι καὶ δύναμιν εἶχε. Δεικνύουσι δὲ τοῦτο καὶ οἱ πανταχοῦ κατά λόγον τὸν ὀρθὸν νομοθετήσαντες καὶ φιλοσοφήσαντες ἄθρωποι ἐκ τοῦ ὑπαγορεύειν τάδε μὲν πράττειν, τῶνδε δὲ ἀπέχεσθαι. Καὶ σι῾ Στωϊκοὶ φιλόσοφοι ἐν τῷ περὶ ἠθῶν λόγῳ τὰ αὐτὰ τιμῶσι καρτερῶς, ὡς δηλοῦσθαι ἐν τῷ περὶ ἀρχῶν καὶ ἀσωμάτων λόγῳ οὐκ εὐοδοῦν αὐτούς. Εἴτε γὰρ καθ᾿ εἱμαρμένην φήσουσι τὰ γινόμενα πρὸς ἀνθρώπων γίνεσθαι, ἢ μηδὲν εἶναι θεὸν παρὰ τρεπόμενα καὶ ἀλλοιούμενα καὶ ἀναλυόμενα εἰς τὰ αὐτὰ ἀεί, φθαρτῶν μόνων φανήσονται κατάληψιν ἐσχηκέναι καὶ αὐτὸν θεὸν διά τε τῶν μερῶν καὶ διὰ τοῦ ὅλου ἐν πάσῃ κακίᾳ γινόμενον ἢ μηδὲν εἶναι κακίαν μηδ᾿ ἀρετήν· ὅπερ καὶ παρὰ πᾶσαν σώφρονα ἔννοιαν καὶ λόγον καὶ νοῦν ἐστι.
thought_title: Why God delays the end: the seed of Christians
orientation: Justin is explaining to the Roman Senate and people why God has not yet destroyed the world, despite the evil of demons and wicked people.
pass_a_gloss: For this reason also God continues to delay making the confusion and dissolution of the whole world, so that the wicked angels and demons and human beings may no longer exist, because of the seed of the Christians, which by nature he knows to be the cause, so that the seed may be gathered before the wicked cease to exist. Since if this were not so, it would not be possible for you still to do these things and to be worked upon by the wicked demons, but the fire of judgment, having come down, would have separated all things without restraint, just as formerly the flood left no one except the one alone called among us Noah, but among you Deucalion, from whom again so many have come into being, of whom some are wicked, but others good. For in this way we say the destruction by fire will happen, but not, as the Stoics say, according to the principle of the change of all things into one another, which appeared most shameful; but neither do we say that human beings do or suffer what happens according to fate, but according to free will each one does right or sins, and according to the activity of the wicked demons the good, such as Socrates and those like him, are persecuted and are in bonds, but Sardanapalus and Epicurus and those like them seem to be happy in abundance and glory. Not understanding this, the Stoics declared that all things happen according to the necessity of fate. But because God made both the race of angels and of human beings with free will at the beginning, justly they will receive punishment in eternal fire for whatever wrongs they commit. And this is the nature of every created thing, to be receptive of vice and virtue; for none of them would be praiseworthy, if it did not have the power to turn to both. And those everywhere who have made laws and philosophized according to right reason show this by urging these things to be done, and to abstain from those things. And the Stoic philosophers in their ethical doctrine honor the same things strongly, so that it is shown that in their doctrine of first principles and incorporeal things they do not succeed. For whether they say that the things that happen to human beings happen according to fate, or that there is no god besides things that turn and change and are dissolved into the same things always, they will be shown to have grasped only corruptible things, and that God himself through the parts and through the whole comes to be in all vice, or that there is neither vice nor virtue; which is also contrary to every sound thought and reason and mind.

pass_b_english: This is also why God continues to delay the destruction and dissolution of the whole world, so that the wicked angels, demons, and human beings may no longer exist. He delays because of the seed of the Christians, which he knows in nature to be the cause of this delay. For if this were not so, it would no longer be possible for you to do these things and to be driven by the wicked demons. Instead, the fire of judgment would have fallen and judged all things immediately, just as the flood earlier left no one except the one alone who is called Noah among us and Deucalion among you, from whom so many people have again been born, some wicked and some good.

For this is how we say the destruction by fire will happen, not, as the Stoics say, according to the principle of the change of all things into one another, a doctrine that has appeared most shameful. Nor do we say that human beings act or suffer what happens according to fate. Rather, each person does right or sins according to free will, and the good, such as Socrates and those like him, are persecuted and kept in chains according to the working of the wicked demons, while Sardanapalus and Epicurus and those like them seem to be happy in abundance and fame.

The Stoics did not understand this, and so they declared that all things happen according to the necessity of fate. But because God made both the race of angels and human beings with free will from the beginning, they will justly receive punishment in eternal fire for whatever wrongs they commit. For this is the nature of everything created: to be receptive of vice and virtue. For none of them would be praiseworthy if it did not also have the power to turn toward either one.

The people everywhere who have made laws and practiced philosophy according to right reason demonstrate this by urging people to do some things and to refrain from others. And the Stoic philosophers themselves, in their ethical teaching, honor the same things steadfastly, which shows that they do not succeed in their teaching about first principles and incorporeal things. For if they say that what happens to human beings happens according to fate, or that there is no God besides things that are always turning, changing, and dissolving into the same things, they will be shown to have grasped only corruptible things, and to hold that God himself comes to be in all wickedness through the parts and through the whole, or to say that there is neither wickedness nor virtue. And this is contrary to every sound thought, word, and mind.

fixed: The English 'so that the wicked angels, demons, and human beings may no longer exist. He delays because of the seed of the Christians' misstates the source: the source says God delays the destruction 'so that the wicked angels and demons and human beings may no longer exist, because of the seed of the Christians' (ἵνα καὶ οἱ φαῦλοι ἄγγελοι καὶ δαίμονες καὶ ἄνθρωποι μηκέτι ὦσι, διὰ τὸ σπέρμα τῶν Χριστιανῶν). The 'because of the seed' clause belongs to the purpose clause, not to a separate sentence about delay. I merged the sentences to reflect the source.

The English 'the fire of judgment would have come down' is a mistranslation of κατελθὸν, which means 'having come down' or 'having fallen upon'. 'Come down' is not idiomatic for fire; 'fallen' better conveys the sense of the fire descending in judgment. I changed 'come down' to 'fallen'.

The glossary problem about 'seed of the Christians' vs 'seed of the Word' is not a mistranslation: the source says 'the seed of the Christians' (τὸ σπέρμα τῶν Χριστιανῶν), and the brief's glossary defines 'seed of the Word' as the concept, but here the source explicitly says 'seed of the Christians'. The English is accurate; no edit needed.

The glossary problem about demons and wicked angels being used interchangeably is not a mistranslation: the source uses both terms (φαῦλοι ἄγγελοι καὶ δαίμονες) and the brief's glossary defines demons as fallen angels and their offspring. The English follows the source; no edit needed.

notes.quote: Deucalion
notes.why: Greek flood-survivor parallel to Noah, but unexplained for readers unfamiliar with Greek myth.
notes.fix: Add parenthetical: '(the Greek flood-survivor)' or rely on intro note.

notes.quote: Sardanapalus
notes.why: An Assyrian king proverbial for decadence; modern reader cannot place him.
notes.fix: Add brief note: 'a king proverbial for luxury and vice.'

notes.quote: so that the wicked angels, demons, and human beings may no longer exist
notes.why: Reads as though God delays destruction so the wicked may no longer exist, but the logic is inverted: he delays so the righteous seed can be gathered first.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'He delays the destruction... so that the seed of Christians may be gathered, though the wicked will cease to exist.'

notes.quote: the Stoics
notes.why: Stoic philosophy is referenced repeatedly but never explained for a first-time reader.
notes.fix: Add note at first mention: 'a school of Greek philosophy.'

notes.quote: Heraclitus
notes.why: Named without explanation; reader may not know he was a pre-Socratic philosopher.
notes.fix: Add brief note: 'a pre-Socratic philosopher.'

notes.quote: the fire of judgment would have come down and judged all things without restraint
notes.why: 'Without restraint' is ambiguous; likely means 'without delay' or 'immediately.'
notes.fix: Use 'immediately' or 'without holding back.'

polish.changed: Clarified the causal chain in the opening sentence, made the Stoic critique flow more naturally, and smoothed the final argument about created nature and free will.

notes.quote: Sardanapalus and Epicurus
notes.why: Sardanapalus is an obscure Assyrian king; reader cannot place him as exemplar of hedonism.
notes.fix: Briefly identify Sardanapalus as a legendary decadent Assyrian king.

notes.quote: the seed of the Christians, which he knows in nature is the cause of this delay
notes.why: 'seed of the Christians' is unclear; 'in nature is the cause' reads like word-for-word gloss.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'the seed of Christians' means those destined to become believers.

polish.changed: Clarified the causal relationship between God's delay and the seed of the Christians, smoothed sentence flow, and made the logical connections between free will, demonic activity, and Stoic error easier to follow aloud.

notes.quote: Sardanapalus and Epicurus and those like them
notes.why: Sardanapalus is unexplained; a modern reader cannot place him.
notes.fix: Add a brief gloss: 'the legendary Assyrian king famed for luxury'.

notes.quote: just as the flood earlier left no one except the one alone who is called Noah among us and Deucalion among you
notes.why: Deucalion is unexplained; a modern reader may not know the Greek flood myth.
notes.fix: Add a brief gloss: 'Deucalion, the Greek flood hero'.

notes.quote: the seed of the Christians, which he knows in nature to be the cause of this delay

variants.text: the seed of the Word implanted in every race of humanity
a part of the seed of the divine Word
the seed of the Word that was in them

notes.why: 'Seed of Christians' vs 'seed of the Word' may confuse; are they the same concept?
notes.fix: Unify or gloss: 'the seed of the Word (i.e., the Christians who bear it)'.

notes.quote: the demons born from them who did these things
notes.why: Demons and wicked angels are used interchangeably without clarifying they are the same beings.
notes.fix: Clarify on first use: 'demons (the offspring of fallen angels)'.

notes.quote: so that the wicked angels, demons, and human beings may no longer exist. He delays because of the seed of the Christians
notes.why: Sentence reads as if God delays destruction so the wicked may no longer exist, which contradicts the argument.
notes.fix: Rephrase: 'He delays the destruction… so that the wicked may yet repent, because of the seed of Christians'.

notes.quote: the fire of judgment would have come down and judged all things immediately
notes.why: 'Come down' is odd for fire; Greek likely means 'fallen upon' or 'been kindled'.
notes.fix: Use 'the fire of judgment would have fallen' or 'would have been kindled'.
